stages.name: Boom and the current account
stages.title: Boom and the current account
stages.sub: Why a fast-growing economy can end up buying more from abroad than it sells.

steps.q: The economy is in a boom, with real GDP growing fast. What happens to households' incomes?
steps.hint: A boom means firms are producing and paying out more than usual.

steps.q: With more income, people buy more of everything, including cars and phones made abroad. What happens to spending on imported goods?
steps.hint: Do people only spend their extra income on home-made goods, or on foreign ones too?

steps.q: Imports are rising while exports are not growing as fast. What happens to the gap between what the country sells abroad (X) and buys from abroad (M)?
steps.right: It gets worse, exports minus imports falls
steps.wrong: It gets better, exports minus imports rises
steps.hint: Recall net exports is X minus M. If M is rising faster than X, what happens to that figure?

steps.q: The value of imports now exceeds the value of exports. What does this mean is happening to money flowing out of the country compared with money flowing in from trade?
steps.right: More money is flowing out than in
steps.wrong: More money is flowing in than out
steps.hint: If people buy more from abroad than foreigners buy from them, which way does the trade money flow lean?
